what_its_for: Ibandronate is used to treat and prevent osteoporosis (thinning and weakening of bones) in women who have gone through menopause. It helps make your bones stronger and lowers your chance of breaking a bone.
how_to_take: Take ibandronate tablets by mouth first thing in the morning, before you eat or drink anything (except plain water). Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of plain water (about 6 to 8 ounces). Do NOT use mineral water, coffee, tea, juice, or milk. After swallowing the tablet, stay sitting upright or standing for at least 60 minutes — do not lie down. Do not eat, drink anything other than plain water, or take any other medicines or vitamins during those 60 minutes.
dosing: The most common dose is one 150 mg tablet taken once a month, on the same date each month. Your doctor may also prescribe a 2.5 mg tablet taken once every day. Follow your doctor's instructions carefully. Your doctor may also recommend taking calcium and vitamin D supplements along with this medicine.
missed_dose: If you take the monthly tablet and miss your dose: If your next scheduled dose is more than 7 days away, take the missed tablet the morning after you remember. If your next scheduled dose is only 1 to 7 days away, skip the missed dose and wait until your next scheduled date. Never take two tablets in the same week. If you take the daily 2.5 mg tablet and miss a dose, skip it and take your next dose the following morning as usual. Do not take two doses on the same day.
storage: Store ibandronate tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep them away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep this medicine in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Do not eat, drink (except plain water), chew gum, or suck on candy for at least 60 minutes after taking your tablet. Do not take antacids, calcium supplements, vitamins, or other medicines within 60 minutes of taking ibandronate, as they can prevent your body from absorbing the medicine properly. Do not lie down for at least 60 minutes after taking the tablet, as this can cause serious irritation or ulcers in your esophagus (the tube connecting your mouth to your stomach). Avoid smoking and drinking too much alcohol, as these can weaken your bones further.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: chest pain, heartburn, or pain when swallowing; new or worsening pain in your hip, groin, or thigh; jaw pain, swelling, or numbness; severe bone, joint, or muscle pain; any unusual thigh bone pain; skin rash, hives, or swelling of the face, lips, or throat (signs of an allergic reaction). Also tell your doctor if you have low blood calcium (hypocalcemia), kidney problems, or any upcoming dental procedures before starting this medicine.
when_it_works: Ibandronate starts working in your bones right away, but you may not feel any difference because osteoporosis usually has no symptoms. It may take several months to years of treatment to see the full benefit of stronger bones and reduced fracture risk. It is important to keep taking it even if you feel fine. Your doctor will monitor your progress with periodic bone density scans.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Ibandronate is not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor if this applies to you. Kidney problems: This medicine is not recommended if your kidneys are not working well (creatinine clearance less than 30 mL/min). Your doctor will check your kidney function before prescribing this medicine. Older adults: Ibandronate can be used in older adults, but they should be monitored closely for side effects. Children: Ibandronate is not approved for use in children.
